name: Hart im Zillertal
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny village between Rattenberg and Schlitters – the perfect starting point for exploring the Zillertal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hart im Zillertal is situated at an elevation of 666 metres in the front Zillertal valley within the district of Schwaz. Covering approximately 35 square kilometres on the sun-blessed eastern slopes directly opposite Fügen and Uderns, the peaceful municipality has a population of around 1,600. Thanks to its elevated hillside location, the village enjoys abundant sunshine and sweeping panoramic views across the broad valley floor. Hart consists of a picturesque central village alongside scattered rural hamlets such as Niederhart, Helfenstein, and Haselbach, ascending toward the rugged peak of the Hamberg at 2,295 metres. Away from heavy transit roads, Hart preserves an unspoilt Tyrolean village ambiance cherished by nature seekers.

History

The earliest documented mention of Hart appears between 1140 and 1147 in the records of the Bishopric of Brixen, referring to estates in loco qui dicitur Harte. The name originates from the Middle High German word hart, meaning a forested hill or wooded mountain pasture. Rural life was historically anchored in livestock farming and timber forestry, thriving on the fertile, sunlit slopes. A cultural landmark of the village is the pilgrimage chapel of the Visitation (Mariä Heimsuchung) atop the Hartberg, built in the 17th century on a serene forest clearing. In the village centre, the Baroque parish church of St. Bartholomew was erected in its present form during the 18th century, showcasing intricate devotional art.

Getting There

By automobile, motorists take the Inntal Motorway A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, then follow the federal highway B169 southward to the Fügen junction. From there, cross the River Ziller eastward via the provincial road, which climbs gently up to Hart in just a few minutes. Train travellers arrive via ÖBB services at Jenbach station and transfer to the scenic Zillertalbahn narrow-gauge railway. Arriving at Fügen-Hart or Kapfing stations, passengers connect to local regional buses or short taxi rides up to Hart. The village is also easily accessible by bicycle or foot via bridges spanning the Ziller River.

Tips

The crown jewel of the local landscape is the Harter Schleier Waterfall (Schleierwasserfall): Plunging dramatically down sheer rock faces with a drop of over 90 metres, it stands as the highest waterfall in the entire Zillertal. The waterfall is reached via a family-friendly Nature and Bird Educational Trail featuring informative displays depicting more than 40 native bird species. Experienced hikers can tackle the rewarding ascent up to the panoramic summit of the Hamberg. In winter, cleared winter walking paths and natural tobogganing provide quiet recreation, while major ski areas Spieljoch and Hochzillertal are just minutes away.
